title: Smart Devices and Personal Data
text:
Smart speakers and fitness trackers are now common in many homes. These devices collect information about our voices, sleep and daily activity. Manufacturers say this data helps them make products more useful and personal. However, privacy researchers warn that such information can reveal much more than people expect.

Companies must follow data protection rules when they handle personal information. In some regions, people have the right to ask for their data to be deleted. Many users, however, never read the long privacy policies that come with new devices. As a result, they may agree to share information without fully understanding how it will be used.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do smart speakers and fitness trackers collect?
options: Information about voices, sleep and daily activity

questions.text: What right do people have in some regions, according to the second paragraph?
options: The right to ask for their data to be deleted
The right to sell their data to companies
The right to change the color of their devices
The right to avoid paying taxes

questions.text: Why do privacy researchers warn about these devices?
options: The data may reveal more personal details than people expect
The devices are too expensive for most families
The devices stop working after one year
The devices can only be used outdoors

questions.text: What can be inferred about users who do not read privacy policies?
options: They may share information without fully understanding the consequences
They always know exactly how their data is used
They refuse to buy any new devices
They have no personal data at all

vocabulary.definition: to make something known that was previously hidden or secret
relating to a particular person and their private life
official plans or rules that an organization follows

paragraph_translations: Alto-falantes inteligentes e pulseiras de atividade física são comuns em muitas casas hoje. Esses dispositivos coletam informações sobre nossas vozes, nosso sono e nossas atividades diárias. Os fabricantes afirmam que esses dados os ajudam a tornar os produtos mais úteis e personalizados. No entanto, pesquisadores de privacidade alertam que essas informações podem revelar muito mais do que as pessoas imaginam.

As empresas devem seguir regras de proteção de dados quando lidam com informações pessoais. Em algumas regiões, as pessoas têm o direito de pedir que seus dados sejam apagados. Muitos usuários, porém, nunca leem as longas políticas de privacidade que acompanham os novos aparelhos. Como resultado, podem concordar em compartilhar informações sem entender totalmente como elas serão usadas.
